what: The Hero is pinned, and the numbered (data-sec) panels sit side by side at their joined widths, then slide left by the scrolled distance (sum of panel widths − viewport width). Scrub 1 makes them follow smoothly with a 1s lag. Several panels with the same number (back·middle·front layers) move together, so a fixed piece placed between them (the group photo in the middle) stands sandwiched between the front and back layers. Pieces with data-speed are pushed an extra (1 − speed) × the moved distance, so they flow at a different rate from the panel and create depth. Pin start and return fire fx:enter and fx:leave.

options.[data-fx-part=section]: Pushed panel (child) — the same data-sec number means the same position, give it a different width (e.g. double) and it stays that much longer
options.[data-speed]: Piece inside the panel — below 1 it moves less than the panel so it feels slower, above 1 faster (original .6~1.4)
options.--fx-pan: Write progress 0–1 on the element — the consumer can bind other things to it with css

use: …
note: Same method on phones (the original also just doubles the panel width on portrait screens)

from.where: index.html .am-kv (hero — seven panels, the second panel is double width on phone, the two layers of group photo running in the center are fixed, floating photos data-speed .6~1.4, scrub 1)
